references.text: Jesus' prayer that the disciples should be where He is repeats the promise of fellowship with Him in His presence.
Jesus promises that whoever serves Him will follow Him where He goes, which reflects the promise of being taken to be with Him.
Paul describes the Lord Himself coming down from heaven to take with Him those who have died in Christ, a direct answer to the promise of gathering the disciples to Himself.
Revelation completes the theme of God's dwelling among humanity, where He Himself is present with His people forever.
The psalm expresses the same longing to dwell in the Lord's house forever, as a parallel picture of the eternal home Jesus promises.
The prophecy that God will create new heavens and a new earth, where there will be joy over what He has made, connects to the preparation of a new place for God's people.
